narrative.overview: Every surface reads like a page out of declassified military hardware: stamps, stencils, chain-of-command eyebrows, classification badges, and terse radio copy. The UI is paperwork from a war that is already happening — hard, functional, cinematic-dark. Orange is the classification color and the only voice of command; everything else is steel and shadow. Density is high but honest: micro-labels are deliberately tiny stencil type, while every value a player acts on is a large mono numeral. Depth comes from black ambient shadow, never colored halos — colored light is reserved for state. Corners are cut with clip-path notches, not rounded; nothing in this system is soft.
keyCharacteristics: Stencil micro-labels (mono, uppercase, tracked wide) against large mono data values
One command color: Muzzle Flash Orange, used at small fractions of any screen
Cut-corner notched silhouettes (clip-path) instead of rounded cards
Black depth shadows; zero-offset glow exists only as functional state feedback
Condensed DIN-family display type over Consolas mono data
Playable over a live 3D night scene — panels are translucent glass, not opaque blocks

rules.name: The 5% Orange Rule
rules.body: Muzzle Flash Orange covers a small fraction of any screen — a rail, a needle, a stamp, one button. Its rarity is the point; bulk orange fills would turn the command color into decoration.

rules.name: The State Light Rule
rules.body: Zero-offset colored glow is allowed only as state feedback — health fill, streak-ready button, compass needle, hitmarker, visible-enemy radar blips. Decorative static glows are banned.

rules.name: The Stencil Rule
rules.body: Wide tracking (0.12em+) belongs to short uppercase labels only. Sentences and body copy read at normal tracking (≤ 0.05em) — wide-tracked paragraphs are a legibility failure, not a mood.

rules.name: The Data Speaks Louder Rule
rules.body: When a label and its value share a panel, the value is mono, large, and brighter than the label ever is.

rules.name: The Night Depth Rule
rules.body: Shadows are black with real offset; they describe physical lift over the night yard. Colored light describes state, never shadow.

dos: Do keep orange rare — rails, needles, stamps, one command button per screen.
Do use cut-corner clip-path notches (12-16px) for command surfaces.
Do render data values in large mono (24-40px) with stencil labels at the 9.5-10px floor.
Do reserve zero-offset glow for state feedback only.
Do keep shadows black, offset, and increasing with importance.
Do keep the 3D view readable — panel blur at 2-4px, no full-screen pattern overlays.
donts: Don't add external fonts, images, or audio — everything is procedural or system-stack.
Don't round cards with large radii; this system cuts corners, it never curls them (max 4px outside touch ergonomics).
Don't add blinking/pulsing dots or decorative animations to static UI.
Don't widen letter-spacing on sentences or body copy (≤ 0.05em there).
Don't drop functional text below 9.5px, or push render resolution below native — sharpness is a product commitment.
Don't use glossy sci-fi neon (blue/purple gamer RGB), gradients as surface fills, or gray-on-gray low-contrast panels.
